reason: Verified in the source and by computed style at 390px. b.css line 34 [data-medium="sheet"] .b-field / [data-medium="full"] .b-field is (0,2,0); the @media (max-width:700px) block at 35-40 and 117-127 is all bare classes (0,1,0), and a media query adds no specificity, so every declaration in it loses. Measured at 390 on owner-flight, owner-editing, publish and desk: .b-field padding 48px 56px 56px, .b-measure padding-left 124px, .b-item left 124px, .b-title 24px, .b-num 148px; owner-empty 120px/56px/130px with a 64px headline. The two named exceptions check out too: .b-ended computes 72px 22px 80px (line 575 beats line 38 on source order, same specificity), and .b-print computes 48px 56px 56px at 1440 as well as 390 because the print element is .b-print.b-field and .b-print (0,1,0, line 627) cannot outrank line 34 at any width, so the print page's own margins are dead everywhere, not just on a phone. The consequence is real, not cosmetic: at 390 the owner measure leaves 154px for a 24px title, .b-title's -webkit-line-clamp:2 clips 94px of content into a 62px box so "Menu tasting at The Orchard" reads truncated, and my collision probe returns exactly the claimed three 12px overlaps on owner-flight at 390 and the same three at 901. The gates do not cover it: interaction-check.mjs runs its collision probe at 1440 per state and at 390 only for state=phone, so both the 390 desk-states case and the 901-1023 two-column band are unmeasured. Not a restatement of anything the gates prove. The fix as written works but is the weaker of the two options, so it is sharpened rather than accepted verbatim.
sharpenedFix: Scope the DESK rules inside a min-width media query instead of prefixing the phone rules with [data-medium]. Wrap all 23 [data-medium="sheet"|"full"] overrides in b.css (lines 34, 64, 81, 116, 141, 150, 153, 166, 177, 193, 208-209, 225-226, 483, 485, 566, 569, 576) in @media (min-width: 701px) { ... } and delete the two @media (max-width: 700px) blocks, keeping only the two declarations that are genuinely phone-specific rather than a restatement of the base: .b-empty and .b-ended at 56px 22px 64px. Why this beats the [data-medium] prefix: (1) it removes the failure mode instead of out-ranking it — a specificity tie can never reopen, whereas the prefix leaves two same-specificity pairs whose outcome depends on the author remembering to keep the phone block last in the file forever, with nothing enforcing it; (2) it is the idiom this same file already uses correctly three times (@media (min-width: 901px) at 305, 497, 631), so it adds no new pattern; (3) it deletes ~8 duplicated literals (line 37 is a verbatim copy of line 30) instead of adding 15 prefixed ones, which is the drift condition that produced this bug; (4) .b-num 96px and .b-emptyTitle 38px fall out of the base values for free, so the two extra declarations the original fix has to hand-add are unnecessary — and so is the hand-add for every medium override written from now on. I simulated it by deleting the medium rules from the CSSOM at 390: .b-field 26px/22px, .b-measure 96px, .b-title 17px, .b-num 96px, .b-empty 22px, .b-emptyTitle 38px, no horizontal overflow, and owner-flight collisions 3 -> 0. Two things this does NOT fix, and the original fix gets one of them wrong: (a) print margins above 700 — do not use .b-print.b-field, which wins only by a second source-order argument; write [data-medium="sheet"] .b-print { padding: 56px 64px 44px; } after line 34 instead, same specificity, later in source, and it reads as what it means; (b) the 901-1023 collisions are not a specificity bug at all but the two-column threshold at line 305 firing before there is room — measured 3 collisions at 901, 1 at 1024, 0 at 1280, so raise that breakpoint to 1280 (or hold the narrow measure scale below it) as a separate change. Keep the gate extension as written: run the collision probe over phone, desk, owner-flight, owner-editing and print at 390, 768, 901, 1280 and 1440, and add the assertion that no .b-field computes side padding above 24px below 700px.
